text: Hemorrhage [Gr. aima , blood, + ragaV , a burst]: Ger. Blutaustritt , Blutfluss ; Fr. hémorragie ; Ital. emorragia . The flowing of blood from a ruptured blood-vessel. Occurring in the brain -- cerebral hemorrhage -- it causes apoplexy. The portion of the brain supplied by the ruptured vessel, or affected by pressure of the escaping blood, being suddenly thrown out of function, causes sudden loss of motion, sensation, and consciousness. Cerebral hemorrhage is frequently the cause of hemiplegia, i.e. paralysis of one side of the body. ( C.F.H. )
